blocks.text: Condo buildings in Mission West

Geography, stated up front: Mission West IS inside the City of Mission — the western side of the city, covering Silverdale and the rural fringe toward Stave Falls and Ruskin — so City of Mission planning, zoning and the flat 10% tax penalty are the frame throughout, and the FVRD rural 5% + 5% regime does NOT apply here. Classification conflict, flagged not smoothed. A presale directory lists Archer Green's ownership as "Condominium" while its own building type is "Townhouse," and MLS listings for the same complex record Sub-Type Townhouse with Ownership Type Freehold Strata. Board-label conflict, flagged not resolved. The Wilson Street parks in are labelled "Mission-West" on the mission-west and mission-mobile-homes feeds and "Stave Falls" on the stave-falls feed, for the same Wilson Street addresses. The label does not change the parks' tenure or the City tax frame.
Streets, schools and getting around Mission West

items.t: The live page headed "Mission West Homes for Sale | Acreages & View Properties" showed 53 results at reading; that count is a feed snapshot, not a market statistic, and the feed spans acreages, detached houses, land, park homes and one townhouse complex. Every first-page card is labelled board sub-area "Mission-West" with a "Mission" mailing address, on streets including Wilson Street, Hayward Street, Olson Avenue, Haffner Terrace, Silverdale Avenue, Keystone Avenue, Gunn Avenue, Nelson Street and Townshipline Avenue.

Board geography: "Mission West" is one of nine sub-areas of the Fraser Valley board community "Mission" (Dewdney Deroche, Durieu, Hatzic, Hemlock, Lake Errock, Mission, Mission West, Stave Falls, Steelhead).
The attached row recorded no Mission West sales, so no attached ratio or attached price statement exists for this sub-area.

The defining plan area on this ground is Silverdale: the Silverdale Comprehensive Planning Area (SCPA) is a 3,440-acre area, sometimes known as Southwest Mission, defined in the City's Official Community Plan and designated for urban growth, with a Central Neighbourhood Plan process and a Master Infrastructure Strategy underway. Development timing, densities and population claims for individual Silverdale listings in feed text are listing copy only: UNVERIFIED as facts for any specific parcel.

The City's Rural Mission Strategy also covers this side of the city — the City describes it as covering the City's rural communities "From Stave Falls, Steelhead and Silverdale to our other rural neighbourhoods," building on the Official Community Plan. Silverdale is therefore both an urban-growth planning area and, in the City's rural strategy, a rural neighbourhood — the two descriptions are the City's own, for different purposes.

Transit — West Coast Express: TransLink's timetable effective January 5, 2026 runs five weekday trains westbound from Mission City Station at 5:25, 5:55, 6:25, 6:55 and 7:25 a.m., arriving Waterfront Station 75 minutes later, and five eastbound trains from Waterfront at 3:50, 4:20, 4:50, 5:30 and 6:20 p.m.; there is no service on weekends or statutory holidays. Mission West is the far side of the city from Mission City Station; station-to-door times for any Mission West address: UNVERIFIED.

Health care: Mission Memorial Hospital, 7324 Hurd Street, consists of a 25-bed medical inpatient unit, a 20-bed PATH unit and a 10-bed Christine Morrison Hospice, and provides primary acute care, outpatient and inpatient, general medicine, laboratory and diagnostic services.

Servicing (City water/sewer vs well/septic) for Mission West acreage lots: UNVERIFIED at parcel level — feed listing text repeatedly references wells, septic systems and community water/septic in the Wilson Street parks, which is listing copy only. Silvermere Lake shoreline: any specific property's dock, moorage, shoreline-tenure or water-access rights: UNVERIFIED — no official source confirms them for a Mission West parcel.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Mission West

items.t: Secondary suites (City frame): all secondary suites in Mission must be registered with the City; a suite is a self-contained living space in a single family home forming part of the same real estate entity, suites are not permitted in townhouses or rowhomes, a new suite goes through the building permit process, and an annual secondary suite fee of $63 plus applicable utility user fees is applied to the property tax notice. The in-house size cap, any owner-occupancy rule and the exact parking count: UNVERIFIED in the research pass.

Mission property tax penalty is a flat 10%: on current taxes left unpaid after the July 2 due date — the City's property tax page states a 10% penalty added to any current balances outstanding on July 3, 2026 (Community Charter ss. 233–234; Mission has no alternative-scheme bylaw). Keep the two regimes explicitly separate: the staged 5% after July 2 plus a further 5% after October 31 belongs to the rural regime (Taxation (Rural Area) Act, s. 11) for FVRD electoral areas outside the City — it does NOT apply to any Mission West parcel. Mission taxes also carry a diking levy on top of the other levies.

Manufactured-home pad rent (MHPTA), for the Wilson Street park homes excluded in: pad-rent increases are capped at 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026, and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027.

blocks.text: Good to know about Mission West

items.t: The board shelf and the live feed disagree, openly. The feed includes land and manufactured product the residential splits do not count the same way; neither source should be quoted as the other.

Silverdale is planned twice, in two different City documents. It is the 3,440-acre Comprehensive Planning Area designated for urban growth and, at the same time, one of the rural communities named in the City's Rural Mission Strategy. A listing that quotes only the growth story — or only the rural story — is quoting half the City's own framing.

Archer Green's unit numbers are not a unit count. Listings show unit numbers into the 150s at 8335 Nelson Street, but no source checked states the complex's total — a buyer (or a page) that turns the highest unit number into a count is inventing a figure. Total: UNCONFIRMED.

The two Wilson Street parks pull in opposite directions from a seniors expectation, and they hide under two board labels. Ruskin Place markets itself as family-friendly with no age restrictions; Triple Creek Estates lists a playground and no pet restrictions with no age rule stated. Search both "Mission West" and "Stave Falls" for Wilson Street homes or listings will be missed — the same addresses carry both labels on different feeds.
Mission West's "highest ratio in Mission" is one sale. It is a thin-shelf signal, not a ranking to build pricing on.

A detached second home on a rural Mission West lot usually starts as a zoning question, not a permit. An in-house secondary suite must be registered with the City (building permit for a new suite; $63 annual suite fee plus utility fees; no suites in townhouses), while a detached coach home or garden cottage is a separate accessory-dwelling question governed by the parcel's zone — and on ALR land the ALC frame caps the second residence at 90 m² or 186 m² by parcel size.

items.t: Official Community Plan: Bylaw 6405-2026, adopted April 21, 2026, replacing and repealing OCP Bylaw 6350-2025. The Silverdale Comprehensive Planning Area is a 3,440-acre area, sometimes known as Southwest Mission, defined in the OCP and designated for urban growth, with a Central Neighbourhood Plan process and a Master Infrastructure Strategy underway; the City's Rural Mission Strategy also covers this side of the city ("From Stave Falls, Steelhead and Silverdale to our other rural neighbourhoods"). Development timing, densities and population claims for individual Silverdale listings in feed text are listing copy only: UNVERIFIED as facts for any specific parcel. Mission's Lougheed Highway Corridor Plan is IN PREPARATION, NOT adopted — Council endorsed Focused Land Use Option #2 on July 20, 2026; no corridor-plan adoption is claimed for the Highway 7 corridor serving this side of the city.

ALR: any Mission West parcel in the Agricultural Land Reserve follows the ALC housing frame — one principal residence at a maximum of 500 m², a suite within the principal only, plus at most one additional residence of 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha) — and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)) ( Whether a specific parcel is in the ALR: UNVERIFIED at parcel level. BC Assessment farm thresholds, where they apply, run in the full three-tier form ($2,500 at 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by October 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

City property taxes — FLAT 10% penalty: City of Mission 2026 property taxes were due Thursday, July 2, 2026, with a 10% penalty added to any current balances outstanding (including unclaimed home owner grants) on July 3, 2026 ( — Community Charter ss. 233–234 plus Municipal Tax Regulation, B.C. Reg. 426/2003, s. 3; Mission has NO alternative-scheme bylaw under Charter s. 235. The staged 5% + 5% pattern is the separate RURAL regime (Taxation (Rural Area) Act s. 11) for FVRD electoral areas outside the City — it does NOT apply to any Mission West parcel. Mission taxes also carry a diking levy. Mission has NO Supreme Court registry — foreclosure mapping for this ground is UNVERIFIED.

Servicing and shoreline: servicing (City water/sewer vs well/septic) for Mission West acreage lots is UNVERIFIED at parcel level — feed text referencing wells, septic systems and community water/septic in the Wilson Street parks is listing copy only. faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Mission West?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board figures showed 8 condos and townhomes listed in Mission West. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Mission West a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In September 2026, condos and townhomes in Mission West had a sales ratio of not published for the month. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Mission West from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 2 condos and townhomes sold in Mission West over those 4 months, out of 37 in all of Mission.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.

faq.q: What did townhomes in Mission West sell for?
faq.a: 9 townhomes sold in Mission West between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $685,000.

faq.q: How long do townhomes take to sell in Mission West?
faq.a: The median was 14 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 98.8% of the last list price (11% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: Are there any apartment condos in Mission West?
faq.a: No — none verified. The named attached stock is Archer Green townhouses at 8335 Nelson Street; the rest of the feed is acreages, houses, land and Wilson Street park homes.

faq.q: Is Archer Green a condo complex?
faq.a: It is a townhouse strata. The presale directory's building type is Townhouse (its "Condominium" ownership label is strata-tenure shorthand), and MLS listings record Sub-Type Townhouse with Ownership Type Freehold Strata, built 2022 by Polygon, with the 8,000 sq ft Archer Club. Buy it with full strata diligence — Form B, depreciation report, bylaws — but do not compare it to apartment condos on form.

faq.q: How did Mission West sell in September 2026?
faq.a: No sub-area median is published for Mission West; Mission's community medians (detached $814,000; attached $430,000) are not Mission West figures.

faq.q: Is Mission West in the City of Mission or in the FVRD?
faq.a: Inside the City of Mission — the page covers the western side of the city, Silverdale and the rural fringe toward Stave Falls and Ruskin — so City planning, zoning and the flat 10% tax penalty apply. The FVRD/Province rural frame used for Durieu and Hatzic Prairie does not apply here.

faq.q: What is the tax penalty if I miss Mission's July 2 deadline on a Mission West home?
faq.a: A flat 10% penalty on any current balance outstanding on July 3, 2026 — not a staged 5% + 5%. The 5% + 5% pattern is the separate FVRD rural regime for electoral areas outside the City. Budget for the diking levy as an additional line on the Mission tax bill.
